info.title: Drive API
info.description: The Drive API provides comprehensive access to Plugsurfing's charging infrastructure network. It enables you to manage users, charging keys, search for charging locations, handle payments, and control charging sessions.

environment.description: API environment - use drive-api-stage for testing and drive-api for production

tags.name: Users

post.description: Activates a charging key for a specific user. The key must exist and be unassigned. Once activated, the key can be used to start charging sessions.

parameters.description: Human-readable identifier written on the rfid card or tag, visualNumber from the charging key reservation.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the user who will own this charging key. Must be a valid user ID in your system.

400.description: The provided query parameters, route parameters or body is invalid.

404.description: User or charging key not found

patch.description:
Modify a charging key's properties. You can change the key's name and enable/disable it. Disabling a key immediately prevents it from being used for charging. Important notes:
- Only non-null fields in the request are applied
- Disabling a key takes effect immediately across all charging stations
- Some CPOs cache key status, so in rare cases it may take a few minutes for the disable action to propagate
- Name changes are purely cosmetic and don't affect the key's functionality

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the charging key - can be either the keyId (internal identifier) or contractId (roaming identifier)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the charging key

400.description: The provided query parameters, route parameters or body is invalid.

404.description: User or charging key not found

409.description: Conflict — can happen when making two requests to update the same charging key in a short period of time

post.description: Find charging locations within a specified radius around a geographic point. The center point, distance, limit, and aggregation settings are passed via query parameters; the request body contains only filters. Use an empty JSON body (`{}`) when no filters are needed. Returns up to 300 locations sorted by proximity to the search center (nearest first). Prices are not included. To get prices for a given location, use Get location by id.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: Latitude of the center point in decimal degrees (e.g. N58°30' is represented as 58.5)

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: Longitude of the center point in decimal degrees (e.g. E014°45' is represented as 14.75)

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Search radius in meters

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of individual locations to return. Not applicable when aggregation is enabled. Use a lower limit for faster response times.

parameters.name: aggregate
parameters.description: Enable result aggregation. Recommended for large search radii to improve response time.

parameters.name: aggregationPrecision
parameters.description: Controls the size of aggregation grid cells. Values range from 2 (largest cells) to 9 (smallest cells). Higher precision means smaller clusters but more data. If not specified, an appropriate value based on the search radius is used.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Supported languages: en, bg, cy, de, es, fi, fr, hu, is, it, lt, nb, nl, pl, pt, ro, sv.

400.description: The provided query parameters, route parameters or body is invalid.

get.description:
Retrieve locations in batches. Locations are returned sorted by last_updated timestamp in ascending order.  Prices are not included, to get prices for a given location, use Get location by id. Best practices:
1. Perform initial FULL PULL by paginating through all locations
2. Perform regular DELTA PULLS using last_updated parameter to get only updated locations
3. Use the last_updated value of the last location in the last page as the starting point for next DELTA PULL
4. Perform periodic FULL PULLS to detect removed locations
5. Use cursor to resume interrupted pulls

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Optional - used to set page size value

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Optional - pass cursor from previous response body to get next page.

parameters.name: last_updated
parameters.description: Optional - when set, only locations updated after this date are returned. example `2024-05-27T10:44:48Z`.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Optional - when set, only locations in these countries are returned. example `DEU` or `DEU,FRA`.

parameters.name: power_type
parameters.description: Optional - when set, only locations having at least one connector with this power_type are returned. possible values: `AC` or `DC`.

400.description: The provided query parameters, route parameters or body is invalid.

post.description:
Start a remote charging session. Important implementation details:
1. Only chargers with REMOTE_START_STOP_CAPABLE capability can be used
2. Allow up to 2 minutes for session to transition from WAITING_TO_START to STARTED
3. Wait at least 1 minute before retrying failed starts
4. Multiple ongoing sessions are possible
5. Subsequent start requests within 60 seconds on same connector are blocked
6. Session events will notify about session status changes
7. If a user has `CREDIT_CARD` payment method, and 3DS challenge mode is set to `CHALLENGE`, then `threeDSClientSecret` might be present instead of `sessionId`, which your frontend needs to prompt the user to sign. After the user successfully signs the challenge, do a second start request!

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the user who will own the charging session

400.description: The provided query parameters, route parameters or body is invalid.

403.description: Forbidden. The user is not allowed to charge, or the connector won't allow remote charging.

post.description:
Stop a remote charging session. Only sessions started remotely (chargingKeyType=virtual) can be stopped remotely. Important implementation details:
1. Session may be stopped locally even if started remotely
2. Events like SESSION_STOPPED or SESSION_COMPLETED may be received without calling stop
3. If stop request fails, allow retrying after a few minutes
4. If session stays in STOP_FAILED, allow starting new session

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the charging session

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the charging session to stop

put.description:
Transfers a charging key from its current fleet to another existing fleet.

**Business rules:**
- Only charging keys that currently belong to a fleet can be transferred.
- The target fleet must belong to the same EMP parent as the source fleet.
- The target fleet must already have an external payment option configured.
- Transferring to the same fleet is idempotent and returns `200 OK`.

parameters.name: keyIdentifier
parameters.description: keyIdentifier provided when creating the charging key

400.description:
Bad request. Possible causes:
- Missing or invalid request body.
- Charging key does not belong to a fleet (`Charging key must belong to a fleet`).
- Target fleet has no external payment option (`Target fleet must have an external payment option`).

example.message: Charging key must belong to a fleet

403.description: Forbidden. The target fleet belongs to a different EMP parent than the source fleet.

example.message: Target fleet belongs to a different EMP

404.description: Source charging key or target fleet not found.

If a user has `CREDIT_CARD` payment method, and 3DS challenge mode is set to `CHALLENGE`, then `threeDSClientSecret` might be present instead of `sessionId`, which your frontend needs to prompt the user to sign. After the user successfully signs the challenge, do a second start request!

403.description: Forbidden. The charging key is not allowed to charge, or the connector won't allow remote charging.

post.description: Stops the given remote charging session. Only sessions started remotely can be remotely stopped.

DriveApiChargingKeyWhitelistType.description:
Defines when authorization of a charging key by the CPO is allowed.
ALLOWED_OFFLINE: CPO should use realtime authorization. But when the CPO cannot get a response from the eMSP, the CPO shall allow the charging key to be used.
NEVER: Only realtime authorization is allowed. CPO shall always send a realtime authorization for any use of this charging key to the MSP.

post.description: Plugsurfing sends session event notifications to the configured webhook URL. Known event names are SESSION_STARTED, SESSION_STOPPED, SESSION_COMPLETE, SESSION_START_FAILED, SESSION_STOP_FAILED, and SESSION_FEE_INCURRING. New event names may be introduced without prior notice. Events are sent once and the receiver response is not used for retries.

parameters.name: X-HMAC-SHA512-Signature
parameters.description: Base64 encoded HMAC SHA-512 signature of the raw request body. Present when HMAC signing is configured.

parameters.name: X-HMAC-SHA512-SignedAt
parameters.description: RFC 3339 timestamp for when the payload was signed. Present when HMAC signing is configured.

400.description: Invalid payload.

500.description: Receiver failed to process the webhook.

post.description: Plugsurfing sends Charging Detail Records (CDRs) when you are set to clear the sessions. If a request does not receive a 200 response (or times out), Plugsurfing retries nightly for up to 7 days using the same requestId for idempotency.

parameters.name: X-HMAC-SHA512-Signature
parameters.description: Base64 encoded HMAC SHA-512 signature of the raw request body. Present when HMAC signing is configured.

parameters.name: X-HMAC-SHA512-SignedAt
parameters.description: RFC 3339 timestamp for when the payload was signed. Present when HMAC signing is configured.

400.description: Invalid CDR payload.

500.description: Receiver failed to process the CDR.
